For synthetic data curation with LLMs, these results do not directly cover curation pipelines or synthetic-data filtering. They mostly address how LLMs change writing style and how personalization or adaptation affects author-style retention, which is relevant if you are curating synthetic text for stylistic diversity or fidelity. LLM rewriting and generation tend to normalize style and homogenize outputs, reducing author-specific signals and stylistic diversity [1, 3, 5, 8, 10].

If your interest is synthetic data for personalized or authorship-sensitive generation, the papers differ in focus: PersonalBench measures whether personalized generation really matches a target author and finds it does not bridge the human-LLM authorship gap [9]; FAVoR proposes a federated method to mitigate author-style homogenization during multi-author adaptation [10]; AVShift finds fine-tuned LLMs benefit from stylistically diverse training data when generalizing across genres [2]. But none of the supplied papers directly studies synthetic data curation as a standalone topic.
